articles.detail: 5 cycles, all 5 completed and deployed in-cycle, avg 10/cycle

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active, no pause gate is set, and every goal metric cleared its target. The standing irritant — selector multi-source floor misses in four of five cycles — is not a supply problem the tunables can reach: the feed delivered 8 to 13 multiSourceStories per cycle, and the selector rejected most on consequence, not on count (a Disney Q3 earnings beat filed as politics, a Mallorca eclipse travel feature rejected for a fourth consecutive cycle, a Trump golf-course arrest filed as economy). Lowering minArticlesInEvent from 10 would add smaller and less-corroborated events, which is the wrong direction for usable multi-source hard news; eventsCount is already at its 50 ceiling and TOP_EVENTS_TO_FETCH is held at 8 by the API token cap. The binding constraint is cluster category-fit, which lives in the selector prompt and is out of scope for daily tuning.
weakestArea: Regional spread is the thinnest goal metric at 5 of 6 regions against a floor of 4 — the only target not cleared with margin. Oceania has now produced nothing for three consecutive days, and Africa's 6 filings against 63 total is the narrowest that region has run this week. The Americas' 21 is also softer than it looks: a third of it is cartel and US-domestic coverage rather than reporting from Latin America itself.
watching: Two Lebanon filings landed the same day — one on stalled talks with continuing strikes, one on the ceasefire fracturing again — and they should be checked for restatement rather than genuine sequence.

The Hormuz lane split and Iraqi oil bypassing the Syrian pumps are the same energy-routing story reaching readers through two desks; yesterday's claims-versus-observation framing on Hormuz is still unresolved.

Drones ran through three categories in one day — China's export controls, the DHL hub shutdown, the Jebel Ali port blasts — which is a single supply-and-security thread being covered as three unrelated economy items.
Mexico's cartel coverage arrived as two halves of one thread: the US targeting a cartel leader and the Sinaloa organisation splitting into open fighting.
Nigeria filed twice on political violence — the Kwara captives released without announcement and the Osun rivals trading killing claims — with no connective reporting between them.

The two eclipse articles filed ahead of the 12 August date remain unpublished; the selector has now rejected the eclipse cluster in four straight cycles, so those two are the only coverage and should be checked against each other before they run.
coverageGaps: Oceania produced nothing for a third consecutive day, and is the only region that regularly drops out of the daily set entirely.
Latin America reached readers almost entirely through organised crime; no political or economic reporting from the region cleared selection.

The economy multi-source floor was missed in three of five cycles — in each case the selector declined to pad with a weak cluster and filled from single-source niche picks instead, which is the right call but leaves economy structurally thin on corroboration.

Event Registry is mis-categorising a visible share of its clusters (earnings filed as politics, a police blotter item filed as economy), which shrinks the usable multi-source pool below what the raw cluster count suggests.
context: The strongest day this week on volume and speed: 63 articles against 52 yesterday, all five cycles completing and deploying in-cycle, and the fastest average cycle in recent memory at 979s (selector 271s, writer 181s, editor 111s). Science recovered from yesterday's flagged narrowing — 11 filings against 7, with Nature, Quanta, New Scientist, STAT, Phys.org and European Spaceflight all back as specialist spines rather than general outlets covering research incidentally, which resolves the two-day trend the last audit called out. Unique sources rose 48 to 53 and top-source share held at 13%. No experiment has been active since 2026-05-26; the queued numerical-density candidate stays queued because scripts/write-prompt.md is out of scope for daily tuning.
